method: Six spot-reviewed complete Italian question/answer loci from museum 1905 source and pinned modern 1912-short transcription. No same-intent merge approved automatically and no original 1912 facsimile collation.

records.rationale: Both ask directly what prayer is; answers define raising mind/soul to God for adoration, thanks and petition.
Both directly ask why our prayers are not always heard and explain that requests may be spiritually unsuitable or made improperly.
1905 Q527 distinguishes sanctifying/habitual from actual grace. The 1912 short questions distinguish sanctifying from sacramental grace, not actual grace.

1905 directly asks if Rosary or other prayers impede fruitful participation at Mass; no equivalent direct question was located in short Eucharist Q316–354. This is not a proof of absence from every other text.
1905 Q984 explicitly advises an evening examination of conscience; short Q359 describes an examination prior to Confession, a related but different context.

1905 Q855 describes separately contracting civil marriage to secure civil legal effects. The later digital short Q409–410 instead state canonical marriage receives civil effects through registration; that regime reflects 1929 Concordat. Not a contradiction attributable to Pius X himself.

source_caveat: Longer 1905 material is papally prescribed regional Catechism, not necessarily Sarto-autograph; short digital Q409–410 contaminated by post-1929 revision.
